dropped.claim: Visteon demonstrates improving gross margins (14.1% in 2025) and strong cash conversion (operating cash flow of $410.0M exceeding net income of $201.0M by 2x), but faces deteriorating top-line trends with revenue down 2.5% to $3.8B in 2025, key customer production volumes declining 1% versus global light-vehicle production up 4%, and structural pricing pressure from annual OEM price reductions that drove a $141M revenue headwind in 2025. The company secured $7.4B in new business awards including expansion into adjacent markets, but awarded business carries no guaranteed volumes and can be terminated without penalty. Operating cash flow declined from $427.0M in 2024 to $410.0M in 2025, and net income fell to $201.0M in 2025 driven by valuation allowance assessment changes that signal potential concerns about future profitability. The net cash position of $488.0M provides balance sheet flexibility, but the company faces concentrated semiconductor supply chain risk, escalating tariff exposure ahead of 2026 USMCA renegotiation, and ties to underperforming OEM customers losing market share. The verdict is Watch rather than Pass because gross margin expansion and strong new business bookings suggest operational competence, but the thesis requires validation that awarded business converts to revenue and that customer production trends stabilize before deeper engagement is warranted.

Awarded business of $7.4B in new wins during 2025 is not guaranteed, as OEM customers do not guarantee production volumes and have the right to terminate arrangements at any time without penalty, meaning actual sales may be substantially less than projected, and the USMCA will be renegotiated in 2026 with escalating tariff risks across Mexico and China operations.
